title: RWD Manager Call: "Closing Mile 11 at 09:00"

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Plant Control Room Conference Bridge

caller.name: Carl Dunning
caller.label: Manager, Prairie Bend Rural Water District

callee.name: Odell Prescott
callee.label: Director, Sterling Bluff Water Department (Ironbark Liaison conferenced in)

transcript.speaker: SBWD Director
transcript.text: Sterling Bluff, this is Odell Prescott. I've got Ironbark's liaison on the bridge with me.

transcript.speaker: RWD Manager
transcript.text: Good, I want them to hear this. We're closing the mile 11 intake at 09:00. Your trajectory, the one the Environmental Unit put out, says 10:50 at the earliest. I'm not cutting it close.

transcript.speaker: RWD Manager
transcript.text: Here's what I've got. No wells. One point one million gallons, the tower and the clearwell together. Six thousand two hundred customers, using about seven-tenths of a million a day. That's maybe a day and a half... if they behave. And they won't once this hits the six o'clock news.

transcript.speaker: RWD Manager
transcript.text: So I need the interconnect opened the other way. I want to buy about half a million gallons a day from you, starting this afternoon. Can you do that?

transcript.speaker: Ironbark Liaison
transcript.text: Sir, this is the Ironbark liaison. We understand the concern, and Ironbark intends to support alternate supply. I'll need to take the specifics back to the command post.

transcript.speaker: RWD Manager
transcript.text: Your people told my operator this morning you'd pay. I'm not running a pump on a handshake. Put it in writing, with a dollar figure and somebody's name on it. Today.

transcript.speaker: RWD Manager
transcript.text: One more thing. Prairie Haven, the nursing home on our line, already called me. They heard it on Facebook. They want to know whether to fill tubs. Who's calling them? Me, you, Ironbark, the county? Because somebody'd better, and they'd better all say the same thing.

transcript.speaker: RWD Manager
transcript.text: I'm at the plant till the gate's shut. Call me back on this number before nine. I need to know if that interconnect water is coming.

voiceStyles.RWD Manager: Man in his late 50s, rural Kansas accent, blunt and fast, a pump running behind him
voiceStyles.SBWD Director: Calm man in his 50s, measured, speaking on a speakerphone
voiceStyles.Ironbark Liaison: Woman in her 30s, polite and careful, slightly hesitant, quiet lobby

instructorNote: Friction inject: the 45-hour figure on Sterling Bluff's plan assumes the connection sends Sterling Bluff 1.5 MGD, so SBWD has to redo its hours of supply with the connection lost and running the other way (a conservation request moves it toward the plan's 70 hours). Watch for three things: the Director decides whether to sell and how much, and calls the dialysis center, the Medical Center and both nursing homes directly; the QI puts funding in writing but leaves both intake decisions to the utilities; and the ENVL logs the RWD closure at 09:00 on the ICS 232.
